title: Edge Case Consolidation Playbook - Seller Lab (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact seller-facing playbook to triage, consolidate, and operationalize unusual inference requests during pilots and early enterprise conversations. This is intentionally pragmatic — scripts, checklists, and minimal slide outlines sellers and SEs can use without deep engineering time.

Background and why this exists:
- We see ~15% of pilot asks that fall outside our standard decision matrix: nonstandard throughput patterns, strict PII constraints, air-gapped workflows, multi-model routing, and mixed latency/accuracy SLAs.
- These conversations often stall because sellers either ask for a long-engineering roadmap or overpromise. This playbook helps the seller + SE quickly categorize the ask, propose a short pilot path, and map fallback/rollback policies.

TL;DR (one-paragraph):
If a prospect raises a nonstandard requirement, run the three-minute triage, categorize into one of four edge buckets (Data Residency, Bursty/Spiky Throughput, Deterministic/High-Accuracy need, Tooling/Integration Gaps), pick the recommended minimal pilot from the matrix below, and use the two-tier fallback script to set expectations. Capture decisions in a one-page pilot spec and route to the Platform COE.

Who should use this:
- Sellers (AEs, SDRs) running pilot qualification calls
- Sales Engineers during technical discovery
- Customer Success for pilot hygiene and handoff

3-minute triage (script):
1) "What does success look like in 30/90 days?" (capture metric)
2) "What are the non-negotiables — data residency, encryption, offline/air-gap, latency?" (capture yes/no)
3) "What is the expected traffic pattern? average QPS and peak burst in short windows?"
4) "Do you have a preferred model family or are you open to our verified variants?"
5) "Who must sign off for a pilot (security, infra, procurement)?"
-- If any question triggers a nonstandard requirement, mark the record as EDGE and proceed.

Edge buckets + recommended first-step pilot (1-page minimal):
1) Data Residency & Compliance (GDPR/CCPA/Healthcare/PFI):
   - Quick pilot: Private deployment sandbox (VPC) with scoped sample dataset; deliver encrypted inference logs, audit sample, and KMS key flow doc. 2-week PoC.
   - Must-have ask: KMS integration or HSM? If yes -> escalate to Private deployments team and surface SLA expectations.
   - Script snippet: "We can start with a scoped VPC trial and show encrypted logs end-to-end. For HSM-level keys, we'll need a brief security intake but we can run a 2-week sandbox while that completes."

2) Bursty / Spiky Throughput (event-driven peaks, unpredictable QPS):
   - Quick pilot: Dedicated capacity micro-pool for peak simulations + cost forecast model (we run replay + synthetic bursts). 3-week pilot including 1 simulated stress day.
   - Must-have ask: sub-100ms tail latency? If yes -> propose low-latency routing + fallback model plan.
   - Script snippet: "We recommend a dedicated micro-pool for peak capacity validation. We'll run a synthetic stress day to align latency SLOs and cost exposure."

3) Deterministic / High-Accuracy Requirements (legal docs, medical triage):
   - Quick pilot: small labeled test set evaluation + gated rollout with human-in-the-loop. 4-week pilot: evaluation -> calibration -> gated production.
   - Must-have ask: human review percent and error budget.
   - Script snippet: "Let's agree a calibration set and an acceptance threshold. We'll instrument confidence scores and run human review for the initial 10k calls."

4) Tooling & Integration Gaps (proprietary pre/post-processing, long-context state sync):
   - Quick pilot: adapter-layer PoC with an integration sandbox, an API shim, and 2 integration patterns (sync webhook + async queue). 2-3 week pilot.
   - Script snippet: "We'll ship a small adapter and integration spec so you can validate end-to-end. If you need an on-prem connector, that becomes an ops ticket but the adapter proves the flow."

Decision matrix (quick):
- If ask involves sensitive keys/HSM -> Private escalation (security review + 2–4 week intake)
- If ask requires sustained >500 QPS -> Dedicated capacity pricing discussion (reserve commit)
- If ask requires sub-100ms P99 -> low-latency region + canary fallback to smaller context model
- If ask requires offline/air-gapped -> Private on-prem offering + Compliance sign-off

Two-tier expectation & fallback script (use this verbatim):
- Buyer question: "Can you guarantee X?"
- Seller: "We can validate X within a scoped pilot and define firm acceptance criteria. For production-grade guarantees we map the requirement to one of our formal offerings (hosted SLA, Dedicated capacity commit, or Private deployment). If constraints force a longer lead time, we'll propose an interim fallback: (A) compatible model variant or (B) degraded SLA window during ramp while we complete integration."

Pricing quick math (seller cheat):
- Baseline hosted: assume $0.02 per 1k tokens for prototyping simplicity (customize per current pricebook)
- Dedicated pilot cost heuristic: 1–2 dedicated GPUs for 3-weeks -> estimate commit delta and show monthly equivalent
- Example line: "If you want to validate 100k inference calls in a week with burst safety, we'll show both hosted-run and a dedicated micro-pool price; dedicated typically reduces per-call cost by 40% at scale but has a minimum commit."

Technical handoff one-pager (what SE captures before routing to Platform COE):
- Customer name + domain
- Edge bucket selected
- Pilot objective metric (e.g., P99 < 250ms, F1 > 0.88, cost per 1k calls target)
- Data sensitivity level + KMS/HSM needs
- Traffic pattern (avg QPS, peak burst: magnitude & duration)
- Integration pattern (sync api / webhook / batch)
- Must-have signoffs and typical path (security / infra / procurement contacts)
- Suggested pilot duration and canary rollback plan

Canary & rollback talking points (short script for execs):
- "We will stage the rollout: pilot -> canary (5%) -> gradual ramp. At each stage we track three signals: latency, correctness/regression (via eval set), and cost delta. We enforce an automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency SLOs are violated more than X% over a 24h window."

Common objections and short counters (battlecard-style):
1) "We can't share data for testing." -> "Offer scoped synthetic or anonymized samples; remote demo on encrypted VPC with a short NDA while we run a sample."
2) "We need 24/7 uptime guarantees." -> "For critical SLAs we recommend Dedicated capacity + subscription SLA; we'll propose a phased plan: dedicated for peak windows, hosted for low-traffic times."
3) "We're worried about model regressions." -> "We configure quality gating with evaluators and automatic rollback policies; include a short eval harness in the pilot."

Mini slide deck outline (6 slides, speaker notes bullets):
1) Title + one-line value proposition (30s)
2) Pilot hypothesis + success metric (1 slide)
3) Edge bucket & recommended pilot (visual matrix)
4) Tech handshake: what we deliver in 2–4 weeks (artifact list)
5) Costs & guardrails (pricing heuristic + rollback)
6) Next steps & signoff (ship pilot spec template)

Meeting agenda template (30-min discovery with SE + buyer):
- 0–5m: intros & success metric framing
- 5–12m: three-minute triage + clarify non-negotiables
- 12–20m: present recommended minimal pilot & tradeoffs
- 20–25m: alignment on pilot owners and signoffs
- 25–30m: next steps, pilot spec action items, tentative timeline

Pilot spec template (one-paragraph to copy into Jira/Confluence):
"Pilot: [customer] — Objective: [metric]. Scope: [data + integration pattern]. Duration: [weeks]. Deliverables: [sandbox access, audit sample, evaluation report]. Acceptance: [thresholds]. Team: [AE, SE, CS, Platform COE]."

Roles & responsibilities (quick):
- AE: commercial alignment, procurement touchpoint
- SE: technical discovery, pilot instrumentation, run stress replay
- Platform COE: capacity planning, security intake triage, pilot environment provisioning
- CS: pilot hygiene, handoff to production

Data capture & follow-up (seller's to-do):
- Immediately after call: create pilot spec in Confluence and link to JIRA-INF ticket
- Upload sample data or sanitize instructions to shared sandbox folder
- Book a kickoff within 3 business days if pilot approved

Examples of real binds and suggested minimal win patterns (anonymized):
- Fintech firm with bursty nightly batch + strict PII: Showed a 3-week dedicated micro-pool pilot with encrypted logs and KMS; converted to dedicated commit after 6 weeks.
- Healthcare startup needing deterministic F1: small human-in-loop gating then automated low-latency canary; required extra instrumentation but converted faster to production.

Open questions & items to flesh out (owner):
- Define a standard pricing template for micro-pool pilots (Sales Ops) -> owner: Marco Diaz
- Create a short NDA template for data-scope-only tests (Legal) -> owner: Sophie Nguyen
- Automate a one-click pilot spec builder in Confluence (Product Ops) -> owner: Jamal Reed

Version notes: first draft focused on being surgical and usable in a live call. Next iteration: convert to a one-slide cheat sheet and a 2-minute promo video for seller enablement.

----
Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this intentionally opinionated; sellers need scripts not options.
- Avoid overengineering in first pass; we can add exact pricebook numbers later.
- Consider a short internal role-play session to surface missing corner cases.
